summary: Bicol International Airport (DRP) is the primary gateway to the Bicol Region in southeastern Luzon, Philippines, situated in Legazpi City, Albay. The airport is famously set against the backdrop of the iconic Mayon Volcano, recognized worldwide for its near-perfect conical shape. It replaced the smaller Legazpi Airport to accommodate growing passenger demand in the region.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Legazpi City center?
A: The airport is located within Albay province, roughly 10-15 kilometers from downtown Legazpi City, with travel times depending on traffic and chosen transport.

Q: What is the main attraction visible from the airport?
A: Mayon Volcano, one of the most active and perfectly shaped volcanoes in the world, is visible from the airport and surrounding areas on clear days.

Q: Which domestic destinations are served from Bicol International Airport?
A: The airport serves multiple domestic routes connecting the Bicol Region to Manila and other major Philippine cities.

Q: When did Bicol International Airport open?
A: The airport was opened in the early 2020s to replace the older, smaller Legazpi Airport as the region's main aviation hub.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride-hailing services like Grab are available at the terminal for trips into Legazpi City and nearby towns. Private car rentals and shuttle services can be arranged in advance for longer trips to destinations like Donsol or Sorsogon. Allow extra travel time during rainy season, as flooding can affect some routes in the low-lying areas around the city.
local_tip: Request a window seat on the left side of the aircraft during landing or takeoff — you'll get a spectacular aerial view of Mayon Volcano's symmetrical cone, one of the most photographed volcanic landscapes in Southeast Asia.
